newsitem.title: UK: World oil prices inch up, led by U.S. gasoline.
newsitem.headline: World oil prices inch up, led by U.S. gasoline.

text.p: World oil prices ended Wednesday firmer following a late rally led by New York's NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures, brokers said.

On London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), the July Brent contract closed up 12 cents on the day at $20.12 a barrel in early trade after NYMEX's prompt unleaded gasoline contract raced ahead in the last half hour of trade to close up over one cent a gallon at 66.40 cents.

Traders said the market was supported earlier in the day by the American Petroleum Institute (API) data issued late on Tuesday which showed that U.S. crude stocks fell by 5.9 million barrels last week.
The API figure was confirmed by weekly data issued by the U.S. Department of Energy on Wednesday showing that crude stocks were off 5.4 million barrels to 318.3 million barrels last week.
Traders said oil market players were also watching Iraq's "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations which comes up for review after June 7.
On Tuesday, diplomats on the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq said everything appeared to be on track for an extension of the deal at the end of the current 180 day period, which began in December.
But they said the U.S. remained cagey about its position.

The deal allows Iraq to export up to $2 billion dollars worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis reeling under U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"We are waiting for the United Nations to come out and say there is an automatic rollover," one trader said.
Traders were mixed on the prospects of some cancellations of some of the Iraqi crude liftings if Iraq exceeds the $2 billion target.

One seller of the Iraqi sour grade Kirkuk said the possibility of cancellations was slim but a trader said dealers were still worried of Iraq being over-subscribed in the first 180 days. "Maybe some barrels won't flow in the last part of May," the trader said.
